_comment: "What it means for <sport>" on the client card's "What your stats mean" page: one line per stat and sport, with examples from that sport. Cricket also has lines per role (cricket_roles, by the card's role code); a cricketer with no role gets the general cricket lines. Fixed text, chosen in code; never reworded by the AI. No numbers, no exercises. Edit the wording here.

football.label: football
football.strength: Strength helps you hold off defenders, win headers and strike the ball with power.
football.symmetry: Even legs let you accelerate and cut equally off either foot, and land evenly after a header.
football.balance: Single-leg control keeps you steady when you plant your standing foot to shoot or pass, and when you change direction.
football.movement: A good deep squat helps you stay low and balanced when you shield the ball or jockey an attacker.
football.mobility: Ankle range lets you stay low when you turn, decelerate and land, and push off powerfully when you sprint.
football.speed: Speed decides who reaches the loose ball first and how quickly you break into space.

padel.label: padel
padel.strength: Strength powers your smash and bandeja, drives the ball off the back glass and holds a low ready position at the net.
padel.symmetry: Even legs let you push off equally to your forehand and backhand side, and land evenly after an overhead.
padel.balance: Single-leg control helps you lunge for a low volley and recover quickly after stretching for a ball off the side wall.
padel.movement: A good deep squat lets you get low for volleys and for balls coming off the back wall while staying balanced.
padel.mobility: Trunk and shoulder range let you rotate fully into a drive or a vibora and reach balls coming off the glass.
padel.speed: Speed decides how fast you get back for a lob and how quickly you cover a drop shot at the net.

cricket.label: cricket
cricket.strength: Strength helps you drive through the line, bowl with pace and throw hard from the deep.
cricket.symmetry: Even legs help you brace your front leg at delivery and push off equally when running between the wickets.
cricket.balance: Single-leg control keeps you stable through your delivery stride and when you field off balance.
cricket.movement: A good deep squat helps a wicketkeeper stay low and lets fielders get down to the ball quickly.
cricket.mobility: Trunk and shoulder range let you rotate through a full bowling action and a full swing of the bat.
cricket.speed: Speed turns ones into twos and gets you to the ball first in the field.

general.label: everyday life and the gym
general.strength: Strength makes lifting, carrying and climbing stairs easier, and lets you train harder in the gym.
general.symmetry: Even legs share the load when you squat, run or climb stairs, instead of one side doing more of the work.
general.balance: Single-leg control keeps you steady on stairs and uneven ground, and when you train one leg at a time.
general.movement: A good deep squat helps you lift from the floor, sit down and stand up with control.
general.mobility: Trunk, shoulder, hip and ankle range help you reach overhead, twist and bend without stiffness.
general.speed: Speed and quickness help you react and move with confidence, in sport and in daily life.

BAT.label: a batter
BAT.strength: Strength lets you drive through the line, hit over the top and keep your shape against the short ball.
BAT.symmetry: Even legs help you push forward or back equally, and run hard between the wickets off either foot.
BAT.balance: Single-leg control keeps your head still over a big front-foot stride and when you play on the back foot.
BAT.movement: A good deep squat helps you get low for the sweep and stay balanced through a long innings.
BAT.mobility: Shoulder and trunk range let you play a full, free swing of the bat and turn into the pull and cut.
BAT.speed: Speed turns ones into twos and gets you home safely when you're backing up.

PACE.label: a pace bowler
PACE.strength: Strength helps you bowl with pace and absorb the force of every front-foot landing.
PACE.symmetry: Even legs share the load of a long spell and help you brace your front leg the same way every delivery.
PACE.balance: Single-leg control keeps you stable through your delivery stride and front-foot contact.
PACE.movement: A good deep squat supports a strong, stable front-leg brace and your follow-through.
PACE.mobility: Shoulder and trunk range let you get side-on, load your action and rotate through to full pace.
PACE.speed: Speed helps you build momentum in your run-up and get to the ball quickly in the field.

SPIN.label: a spin bowler
SPIN.strength: Strength lets you put revolutions on the ball and repeat your action over long spells.
SPIN.symmetry: Even legs help you pivot on your front foot the same way every ball.
SPIN.balance: Single-leg control keeps you steady as you pivot over your front leg at release.
SPIN.movement: A good deep squat helps you stay balanced through your follow-through and get down quickly for return catches.
SPIN.mobility: Shoulder and trunk range let you rotate fully through your action to spin the ball hard.
SPIN.speed: Speed helps you get across for return catches and cover ground in the field.

ALL.label: an all-rounder
ALL.strength: Strength powers your batting and your bowling, and keeps you going across a long day.
ALL.symmetry: Even legs help you push off equally between the wickets and brace the same way when you bowl.
ALL.balance: Single-leg control keeps you stable in your front-foot stride with the bat and in your delivery stride with the ball.
ALL.movement: A good deep squat helps you get low with the bat and through your bowling follow-through.
ALL.mobility: Shoulder and trunk range give you a full swing of the bat and a full bowling action.
ALL.speed: Speed turns ones into twos and gets you to the ball first in the field.

WK.label: a wicketkeeper
WK.strength: Strength helps you hold a low stance through every ball and dive to take the edge.
WK.symmetry: Even legs let you move and dive equally to your left and right.
WK.balance: Single-leg control helps you stay steady as you shift and take the ball wide of you.
WK.movement: A good deep squat lets you stay low and comfortable in your stance all innings.
WK.mobility: Hip, ankle and shoulder range let you stay down longer and reach the ball wide of your body.
WK.speed: Speed helps you get up to the stumps and move quickly for a run-out or a catch.
